Mr. Amin further submits that admittedly the defendant No. 4 is in possession and the trial Court, the Appellate Court as well as the Revisional Court nowhere in the Judgment held that the plaintiff was in possession in plot No.6428 before dispossession. So it is clear that the plaintiff never got any possession of the suit plot No.6425 and admittedly the defendant No.4 has been possessing the suit Plot No.6428 as homestead and as such the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division committed error of law is not holding that in a case of khas possession the plaintiff must prove his possession prior to file the suit." 

 9. From the plaint, it appears that the plaintiff prayed for declaration of title to the suit land and for recovery of khas possession. The plaintiff claimed title to the suit land on the basis of registered sale deed executed by Gulejan in his favour on 21.05.1979. The plaintiffs further case was that after purchase of the suit land, he got possession thereof and of the two suit plots, he was using the homestead on Plot No.6428 for his own men and another plot by cultivation. In this connection, it may further be stated that initially the suit was filed for declaration of title and confirmation of possession. Subsequently, prayer was added for recovery of khas possession. Both the Courts below believed the plaintiffs case that during pendency of the suit, the defendants dispossessed him. Although both the Courts below concurrently found that the kabala of the defendant was executed much later than the kabala of the plaintiff, yet on the insistence of Mr. Nurul Amin we have gone through the evidence on record, both oral and documentary, particularly, the evidence of the DWs. The reason for such approach of us was that admittedly the deed of the plaintiff by Gulejan was registered much earlier than the deed of the defendant. There is a presumption of correctness of the judicial and official Act in view of the provision of clause (e) of section 114 of the Evidence Act. The plaintiff in his plaint as well as in his deposition categorically asserted as to his acquisition of title to the suit land by virtue of his kabala from Gulejan dated 21.05.1979 and the contesting defendant did not at all challenge the deed of the plaintiff as fraudulent. The defendant did not also deny the fact that the deed of the plaintiff was not executed and registered by Gulejan. We like to observe that though section 114(e) of the Evidence Act has given a presumption as to the official Act and in the instant case, the deed of the plaintiff was registered on 21.05.1979, the contesting defendant in order to take the benefit of section 47 of the Registration Act took the plea that his deed was executed on 30.04.1979, though was registered on 16.07.1979.
